card_text: The buzz cut from Hobbs: the cut that asks the least of you between 80-minute drives.

seo.title: Buzz Cut for Hobbs, NM | Divinely Faded, Carlsbad
seo.description: Buzz, crew and high and tight cuts for Hobbs, cut in Carlsbad 70 miles west. A cut for rotations and hard hats, with the longest gap between trips.

paragraphs: One clipper length over the whole head, a fade climbing the sides and a squared-off line-up at the front. I cut it in Carlsbad, roughly {{city:hobbs.drive_min}} minutes (OpenStreetMap routing) from a driveway in Hobbs by way of {{city:hobbs.route}}.
If your week belongs to a rig, a plant or a field, this is the cut that needs the least from you between visits.

blocks.heading: Even growth means a longer gap.
paragraphs: When every haircut costs you {{city:hobbs.drive_min}} minutes each direction, the cut that grows out evenly wins. On a buzz the top barely changes as it lengthens; what blurs is the fade and the squared front, and I'll tell you in the chair roughly when they'll start to go.

About {{city:hobbs.mining_ag_jobs_pct}} of employed Hobbs residents work in mining, oil and gas or agriculture (Census ACS 2023). On a rotation, book the trip for a day off rather than after a shift; Saturday runs 8 AM to 2 PM.

blocks.heading: Nothing to flatten, nothing to fix.
paragraphs: A buzz comes out from under a hard hat the way it went in: no part to re-set, no top to lift. All that matters after a shift is whether the outline is still clean.

blocks.heading: Short, shorter, bare.
blocks.lead: Three bookings, depending on how far down you go.

items.title: Essential Haircut
items.body: Buzz, crew or high and tight, fade set where you want it, neckline taken clean with a straight razor.

items.title: Signature Cut
items.body: The same short cut with the beard trimmed or lined up, then a hot towel. With hair this short, the beard carries the look.

items.title: Head & Beard Shave
items.body: All the way bare: a precision head shave and beard shave with hot towels and an aftershave balm.

blocks.heading: Buzz cut questions from Lea County.

items.q: How often will I be making the drive from Hobbs for a buzz cut?
items.a: Less often than for most cuts, since the length grows evenly; the fade and the line-up set the pace. Ask me in the chair.

items.q: Buzz, crew or high and tight for shift work?
items.a: Any of the three. A crew cut keeps a bit more on top if you're unsure about your head shape; a high and tight shows the outline most.

items.q: What do the three short cuts look like?
items.a: The buzz cut page explains buzz, crew and high and tight side by side, with a photo from my chair.
